summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with HIV/AIDS (CD4 count of 6), end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of herpes zoster ophthalmicus presented with worsening right-sided headache, dizziness, and facial rash after self-discontinuing gabapentin. She was hypotensive on arrival and received fluid resuscitation, which improved her blood pressure. Workup showed no acute intracranial abnormality on CT, and ophthalmology found no active eye infection. A brief episode of atrial fibrillation resolved spontaneously. She was treated for presumed post-herpetic neuralgia with amitriptyline, eosinophilic folliculitis with fexofenadine, and restarted on PJP and MAC prophylaxis due to her severely suppressed immune system. She tolerated hemodialysis during admission with transient hypotension managed with fluid bolus. Her condition stabilized, and she was discharged home with medication adjustments and follow-up planned in nephrology, infectious disease, and dermatology.
